feedback.problem:
The number of subscribers $S(t)$ to a certain site's e-mail news service after $t$ weeks can be modeled by the differential equation

$$
\frac{\text{d}S}{\text{d}t}=0.01S.
$$

If the site's e-mail news service currently has $10\,000$ subscribers, calculate the number of subscribers after $10$ weeks. Round your answer to the nearest integer.
feedback.worked_solution:
We model the number of subscribers using the differential equation

$$
\frac{\text{d}S}{\text{d}t}=0.01S.
$$

The solution to this equation is

$$
S(t)={S}_{0}\,{e}^{0.01t},
$$

where ${S}_{0}$ is the initial value.

We're told that the service currently has $10\,000$ subscribers, so we have ${S}_{0}=10\,000.$

Therefore, the number of subscribers $S$ at time $t$ is

$$
S(t)=10\,000\,{e}^{0.01t}.
$$

Finally, to find the number of subscribers when $t=10,$ we substitute $t=10$ into the above, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}S(10) & =10\,000\,{e}^{0.01\cdot 10} \\  & =10\,000\,{e}^{0.1} \\  & ≈11\,051.71\end{aligned}
$$

Rounding our answer to the nearest integer, we conclude that the number of subscribers is $11\,052$ after $10$ weeks.
